characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Crossbeam instrument (XB 1540, Carl Zeiss SMT AG, Germany), using a recently developed EBSD-based set-up to obtain ECCI images under controlled diffraction conditions
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 0.2 true strain the grain interior of the long annealed 2Al steel consists mainly of dislocation cell blocks with an average size of 275 ± 50 nm; a uniform distribution of coarse intergranular M3C-type carbides (~1 µm wide × 3 µm long) decorates grain boundaries and annealing twin interfaces; deformation twin bundles form and impinge on the carbides.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Longitudinal sections (observation direction perpendicular to the tensile axis)
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the deformation structures (dislocation substructures, cell blocks, twins) and distribution of intergranular carbides

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Phillips CM20 microscope; thin foils prepared by electropolishing in 30% nitric acid in methanol at −30 °C and 10 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM observations of the deformed high-Mn steels (general method statement for the 2Al and 8Al steels studied).
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the deformation structures and precipitation state

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zwick ZH 100 tensile machine; cylindrical samples with gauges of 6 mm diameter and 40 mm length
characterization_methods.key_findings: Long annealed 2Al (650 °C/72 h): YS = 400 MPa, UTS = 850 MPa, UE = 35%, with a single strain hardening regime.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, initial strain rate 5 × 10^-4 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure mechanical properties and study microstructural evolution as a function of strain
characterization_methods.technique: Tensile testing (including tensile testing to failure and interrupted tests to different strain levels)

analytical_models.equation_role: Estimates the twinning stress from the twin boundary energy and Burgers vector
Relates the flow stress contribution of the dislocation substructure to its size
analytical_models.model_note: Δσ = GMKb/D; used to describe the contribution of the dislocation cell blocks (grain interior, area 1) to the flow stress of the long annealed 2Al steel.

analytical_models.equation_role: Describes the long annealed 2Al steel as grain interior (area 1) plus grain boundary carbide area (area 2)
analytical_models.model_note: Area 1 (grain interior, γ solid solution with dislocation substructures) controls the strain hardening; area 2 (coarse intergranular M3C-type carbides, precipitation γ → γ0 + M3C) mainly contributes to material damage; area 1 is larger than area 2.

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Thermodynamic calculations by Chin et al. [23] on the stability of carbides in the Fe–Mn–Al–C system (used to identify the intergranular carbides as M3C-type)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The estimated twinning stress (~670–750 MPa) is compared with the observed activation of deformation twinning in the long annealed 2Al steel.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: impingement of deformation twin tips on coarse intergranular M3C-type carbides
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The impingement of twin tips on coarse intergranular M3C-type carbides produces local shear stress concentrations at carbide interfaces, enhancing an intergranular fracture mode; fracture occurs at a macroscopic true stress of 1150 MPa.

interfaces.phase_evolution: In the grain boundary area (area 2), segregation of solute elements (mainly carbon) to grain boundaries results in precipitation: γ phase → γ0 phase + intergranular M3C-type carbides; the grain interior (area 1) remains essentially in the solid solution state (γ phase).
interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocation substructure evolution: the strain hardening of the long annealed 2Al steel is controlled by dislocation substructure refinement (Taylor lattice structures, dislocation cells and cell blocks), the same evolution that governs the first hardening stage of the short annealed sample; the high carbon content (1.2 wt.%) and its role in solute carbon/dislocation cross-slip is invoked for the substructure formation.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Within the 2Al steel, the long annealing treatment (650 °C/72 h) leaves yield strength nearly unchanged (YS 400 MPa vs 420 MPa) but strongly reduces uniform elongation (UE 35% vs 75%) relative to the short annealing treatment (450 °C/1 h); both annealing states exhibit identical flow behaviour (multiple-strain hardening with a slope change near 15% strain).

processing_steps.method: melted in an induction furnace under Ar atmosphere and cast to round bars, 25 mm in diameter

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Annealing treatments were performed between 450 and 650 °C; this sample corresponds to the 650 °C/72 h long annealing condition specific to the 2Al steel.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical tensile samples, gauge 6 mm diameter and 40 mm length

strain_hardening_rate.value: single hardening regime ending at ~1.3 GPa near 1100 MPa true stress

precipitates.distribution: uniform distribution along the grain boundaries and annealing twin interfaces

microstructure_list.region: grain boundaries and annealing twin interfaces

defects.type: deformation twins / twin bundles containing several deformation twins

structures.overall_structure: The long annealed 2Al steel (650 °C/72 h) consists of a grain interior essentially in the solid solution state (γ phase) whose deformation proceeds by dislocation substructure evolution, together with a uniform distribution of coarse incoherent intergranular M3C-type carbides along grain boundaries and annealing twin interfaces; at intermediate-to-high stresses deformation twinning develops and twin bands impinge on the intergranular carbides.

unmapped_findings: Fracture of the long annealed 2Al sample (650 °C/72 h) occurs at a macroscopic true stress of 1150 MPa, which corresponds to the onset of the second hardening regime of the short annealed alloy (b0025).

The strain hardening of the long annealed 2Al steel exhibits a single hardening regime that exactly overlaps the first hardening regime of the short annealed alloy up to a true stress of about 1 GPa; the slope of the flow curve changes at about 15% strain with a still-positive slope, indicating a multiple-strain-hardening behavior (b0011, b0019).

The size of the dislocation substructure in the long annealed 2Al steel (cell block average size 275 ± 50 nm at 0.2 true strain) is the same as that in the short annealed 2Al steel strained to the same stress level (270 ± 70 nm at true stress of 950 MPa) (b0019).

Because the short annealed alloy is in the solid solution state (γ phase) and both alloys contain a similar YS, the grain interior of the long annealed 2Al steel is concluded to remain essentially in the solid solution state at the 650 °C/72 h annealing condition (b0019).

Under the annealing conditions studied, deformation twinning in the long annealed 2Al steel does not result in a further hardening regime but activates a damage mechanism triggered by twin–intergranular M3C-type carbide interactions, limiting elongation (UE = 35%) (b0025).
